title: Learn to Keep People Dependent on You
hook: The dental practice on the table makes Paula see dependence before anyone names it.
counterintuition: The weak reading turns this into a pose. The stronger reading asks how dependence changes incentives, status, and timing in the room.
tryThisNow: Before sending the next message, remove one sentence that exposes too much too soon and replace it with a concrete cue that protects dependence.
keyTakeaway: Make your usefulness structural enough that removal becomes costly.

breakdown.fastRead:

examples.scenario: Behind the classroom desk, attorney Paula turns over a dashboard as the learn dashboard sits in view. The sterilizer hums behind the front desk while three hygienists wait for the 90-day recall list. Paula must decide whether to keep fixing gaps invisibly or turn the color-coded schedule, lab pickup times, and insurance limits into one shared grid that every morning huddle now needs.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: Practice reading dependence before you act. The skill is to make make your usefulness structural enough that removal becomes costly in a visible, bounded way instead of drifting into hoarding everything or sabotaging others.

ifThenPlans.plan: If a work decision exposes dependence, then change the first visible artifact or sequence before making the argument.
If the other side can resist the obvious claim, then make indispensability visible through the setup first.
If the move could become hoarding everything or sabotaging others, then narrow it to one concrete action and one clear limit.
If people are watching for status, risk, or advantage, then decide what the room should see first and what should remain quiet.
